rule: Instinct is permanent, asked for, the engine fallback, planned, gated on one commit, and wave delegations stay safe
description: P3 coupling inside plugin/agents/overlord.md. The source pin carries Instinct's standing claim: it is a named, permanent delivery path beside the script engine, so rewording it into a temporary path is loud (ADR-0039 decision 2). Three consumer pins carry the path-choice rule for a standard-delivery request that names neither path, one per clause: the discriminating condition (names neither the engine nor Instinct), the exemption (a request carrying a working_branch.base ref takes the engine without asking, which keeps an unattended overlord from stalling on a question), and the obligation (otherwise ask the user which to use). Three consumer pins carry the engine fallback in the Engine section (ADR-0039 decisions 3 and 4): a refused or blocked standard-delivery launch runs on Instinct, condition and obligation in one pattern; a started standard-delivery run that failed or ended blocked continues on Instinct from the branch's current git state without asking the user; and Instinct never relaunches the engine. Four consumer pins carry Instinct's run obligations, each on its key terms: a plan before any edit, from cerebrate or supplied by the user; the PR opened only on a commit that validation and local review both passed on, condition and obligation in one pattern; a commit made after a gate passed reruns that gate; and anything else decided per Stop Conditions. Three consumer pins carry the Parallel Delegation Safety section: its heading together with its opening sentence, so a heading rename is loud even though the section is also cited by name elsewhere in the file, and the two must-forbid rules (git writes, repo-global mutations), each pinned on its subject and its obligation. Honest residual: pins claim word sequences only, never meaning. A rewrite elsewhere in the file that contradicts a pinned clause stays green, and a citation of the section from another file is not checked. Not pinned here: the Engine sentence and the Tier A bullet that cite the path-choice rule, the fallback's final-report, stop-rule and user-stopped clauses (tests/workflow-scripts/overlord-contract.test.mjs reads the Engine fallback paragraph), the local-review skip exemption, the working-branch, delegation, molt and post-PR watch obligations of Instinct, and the sentence that sends run-ledger writes to the final report.

source.pattern: Instinct is a named, permanent delivery path beside the script engine

consumers.pattern: selects `standard-delivery` and the request names neither the engine nor Instinct
take the engine if the request carries a `working_branch.base` ref
otherwise ask the user which to use
If a `standard-delivery` launch is refused or blocked (denied, not found, or workflows turned off), say so in one line and run the request on Instinct
run that started, then failed or ended blocked, continues on Instinct from the branch's current git state without asking the user
a plan before any edit, from `hivemind:cerebrate` or supplied by the user
only on a commit that validation per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/definitions.md` (Validation Procedure) and local review both passed on
A commit made after a gate passed reruns that gate
Decide anything else, such as order, failures and questions, per `### Stop Conditions`

## Parallel Delegation Safety

These rules hold for every wave of parallel delegations
Each wave delegation must forbid git writes
Each wave delegation must forbid repo-global mutations
